# Go Objects

<!-- Generated by npm run docs; edit scripts/README.template.md. -->

**Query and transform objects, update nested paths, clone object graphs and traverse deep structures.**

[![Source line coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-100%25-brightgreen.svg)](#development)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-100%25-brightgreen.svg)](docs/API.md)

- **Version:** [{{VERSION}}](CHANGELOG.md)
- **Licence:** [{{LICENSE}}](LICENSE.md)

Query own properties, transform records, read and update nested paths, or copy supported object graphs with their descriptors and shared references. An optional wrapper composes the same utilities. Mutable operations change shared input data; immutable path helpers copy only the edited path.

No runtime dependencies. TypeScript declarations included.

**[View full API documentation](docs/API.md)**

## Installation

Using npm:

```sh
npm install go-objects
```

Using Yarn:

```sh
yarn add go-objects
```

### Runtime support

| Environment | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CommonJS    | Node.js {{NODE_MINIMUM}} or later, including supported direct function imports.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ES modules  | Node.js 13.7.0 or later, or 12.17.0+ within 12.x; default, named and direct imports use the native ESM graph.                                                                                                                                                              |
| Browser     | ES2017-capable engines (plus ES module support for ESM entries) with standard features including `Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet`, `Reflect` and `Symbol`. Readable/minified UMD and standalone ESM bundles are supplied; no legacy-browser support or global polyfills. |

CommonJS is verified on Node.js 8.0.0 and later. Development, documentation generation and verification require Node.js >=22.16.0. Optional BigInt, BigInt typed arrays, AggregateError and newer buffer/regex features are supported only when the host provides them; their absence does not prevent unrelated APIs from loading. No global polyfills are installed.

The full browser gate exercises Chromium, Firefox and WebKit offline with readable and minified bundles and the static ESM graph. The browser runner also accepts `--browser firefox` and `--browser webkit` when those Playwright engines are installed. The README script-tag example is also loaded with its exact-version URL intercepted using candidate bytes. These checks do not verify public CDN availability, CSP or the Safari application. Optional built-in types follow the [clone support and opaque-value policy](docs/API.md#shallow-and-deep-cloning-1).

## Usage

### ES modules

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { get } from 'go-objects';

console.log(get({ account: { active: true } }, 'account.active'));   // => true
```

The callable default namespace also remains available, including wrapper pipelines:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import Objects from 'go-objects';

Objects({ profile: { name: 'Michael' } }).get('profile.name').unwrap();   // => 'Michael'
```

### CommonJS

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
const Objects = require('go-objects');
const { get } = Objects;

console.log(get({ account: { active: true } }, 'account.active'));   // => true
```

Other utilities use the same import pattern. For example, clone a graph before changing nested data:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
const Objects = require('go-objects');
const { get, deepClone } = Objects;

const user = { profile: { name: 'Michael' } };
get(user, 'profile.nickname', 'Not provided');                   // => 'Not provided'
const copy = deepClone(user);
copy.profile.name = 'Updated';
user.profile.name;                                               // => 'Michael'
```

### Function subpaths

Each function subpath provides named and default ESM exports of the same function:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import get, { get as namedGet } from 'go-objects/get';

get === namedGet;                                                // => true
get({ account: { active: true } }, 'account.active');             // => true
```

Direct function imports are also supported:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
const get = require('go-objects/get');

get({ account: { active: true } }, 'account.active');            // => true
```

`go-objects/get` selects native ESM for `import` and CommonJS for `require`. The legacy `go-objects/src/get` and `go-objects/src/get.js` paths remain supported, as does the explicit `go-objects/esm/get.mjs` ESM path. Internal modules and the wrapper implementation file are not public subpaths. Modern Node enforces this through the export map; older Node releases do not enforce export maps. Physical function entry files preserve direct CommonJS imports on Node 8.

The ESM root is static and tree-shakeable, but native Node loads its full dependency graph. Use direct function imports to minimise native-Node loading. CommonJS and ESM are separate instances; their functions and wrappers need not share reference or `instanceof` identity.

### Browser

Load the browser bundle directly from jsDelivr, or save it to host on your own site. Neither option requires npm:

- [Minified bundle](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{{NAME}}@{{VERSION}}/dist/go-objects.min.js)
- [Readable bundle](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{{NAME}}@{{VERSION}}/dist/go-objects.js)

To save a bundle locally, right-click its link and choose **Save link as…**. Opening a link normally displays the JavaScript file in your browser.

These links use version {{VERSION}} and stay on that version when newer releases are published. The example loads the bundle from jsDelivr; to host it yourself, replace the script URL with your saved file’s path, such as `./dist/go-objects.min.js`.

The readable `dist/go-objects.js` and minified `dist/go-objects.min.js` files expose `Objects` and support script tags, AMD and CommonJS. Both include source maps and licence notices. Either filename can be used in this example.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{{NAME}}@{{VERSION}}/dist/go-objects.js"></script>
<script>
  const { get } = Objects;

  console.log(get({ account: { active: true } }, 'account.active'));   // => true
</script>
```

For a standalone ES module:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```html
<script type="module">
  import { get } from './dist/go-objects.mjs';

  console.log(get({ account: { active: true } }, 'account.active'));   // => true
</script>
```

UMD exposes `Objects` and also supports AMD/CommonJS loaders. Both standalone bundles contain the complete library. The static `index.mjs` and `esm/` tree can also be served together.

## Behaviour

### Property and matching rules

Most collection operations snapshot own enumerable string keys, followed by symbols. Reverse variants visit that complete list backwards. Deleted properties are skipped and newly added keys are not visited; `pick` follows its requested key list instead. Inherited properties are excluded. Getters and callbacks may run when values are read.

Literal matching uses SameValueZero: `NaN` matches itself, signed zeros match and objects compare by identity. A function matcher is always a predicate; use a predicate such as `value => value === targetFunction` to match function identity.

### Mutation and immutable updates

Mutating path and match helpers return previous values or deletion success, rather than the updated object. Writes may partially complete before an error. Path mutation rejects unsafe segments and forbidden destinations, and never traverses or replaces accessors. Deletion can remove a configurable final accessor without invoking it.

Immutable helpers return an updated root or the original root for a no-op. They copy only the edited path; untouched aliases and cycles can still refer to the original graph. Use [deep cloning](docs/API.md#shallow-and-deep-cloning-1) when a full supported-data copy is needed.

### Traversal and cloning limits

Deep traversal is pre-order, excludes the root callback and expands each supported container once. `deepFilter` prunes rejected branches; unvisited branches and aliases may retain data. It is **not an authorisation or complete redaction boundary**.

Cloning preserves descriptors, including non-enumerable properties. Unsupported values remain references by default, or throw under the strict policy. Native Error stack materialisation may invoke `Error.prepareStackTrace`. See [shared contracts and examples](docs/API.md#behaviour).

### Wrapper pipelines

`Objects(value)` and `new Objects(value)` create independent wrappers. Every utility method returns a new wrapper. `unwrap()` returns the current pipeline value; `result()` exposes the last standalone return. Explicit mutations still affect shared input data. See [wrapper behaviour](docs/API.md#wrapper-behaviour).

## TypeScript

TypeScript declarations are included; no separate `@types` package is required.

TypeScript 5.3.3 or later is supported, with checks on 5.3.3 and {{TYPESCRIPT_VERSION}}. Declarations cover the callable namespace, all utilities and direct imports, browser formats and wrapper pipelines.

Known keys and segment tuples preserve useful types. Dynamic or parsed string paths stay conservative. Mutable writes must satisfy the existing schema; immutable helpers support intentional schema changes. See [typing behaviour and examples](docs/API.md#typescript).

## Performance

Shallow operations enumerate own keys; deep operations visit eligible property edges and expand shared containers once. Direct imports avoid loading unrelated utility families. Tree-shaking is checked with the pinned esbuild tool.

See the [performance guide](https://github.com/koyote130708/go-objects/blob/main/docs/PERFORMANCE.md) for historical measurements, comparison commands and limitations.

## Migration

Version 3 introduced persistent wrapper bookkeeping and stricter argument/type validation. Retain the wrapper returned from each fluent operation. Read the [migration guide](docs/MIGRATION.md) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) before upgrading.

## Development

Use npm with Node.js >=22.16.0 for development:

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm test
```

`npm run build` regenerates the README and API reference, then creates the complete consumer package. Edit `scripts/README.template.md` and `scripts/API.template.md`; the full reference supplies the README summary. `npm run docs` regenerates just the documents. `npm run test:docs` checks both documents, links, complete API entries, examples and TypeScript snippets.

`npm test` runs runtime regressions. `npm run verify` builds and packs one candidate, then checks lint, formatting, documentation, coverage, declarations, generated artifacts, installed imports, runtimes, tree-shaking and bounded mutations. `npm run verify:all` adds Chromium, Firefox and WebKit checks for both readable and minified browser bundles. Install Python Playwright and all three engines using the [contributor guide](https://github.com/koyote130708/go-objects/blob/main/docs/project-testing.md#setup-and-gates). The guide also covers build recovery and focused commands.

The coverage badge reports source-line coverage. The verification thresholds are 100% lines/functions and 99% branches; coverage complements behavioural tests. The docs badge counts complete utility, callable and wrapper-accessor entries.

Generated consumer files live in `package/`; the repository is private development tooling. Run `npm run verify:all` to build, pack and validate one consumer tarball in `artifacts/`; `npm run pack:package` performs only the build and pack. Publish the reviewed tarball, not the repository root. To check an existing tarball on another runtime, run `npm run test:runtime -- --node /path/to/node --tarball /path/to/go-objects.tgz`; add `--esm` for Node.js 13.7.0 or later, or 12.17.0+ within 12.x.
